key_insight: Combining physics-based simulation and neural networks mapped HDPE friction stir welding quality, identifying 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating as optimal among the tested conditions.
engineering_relevance: Bottom preheating can reduce plunge loads and thermal gradients, helping engineers select more stable welding conditions and avoid void defects.
method: Simulated temperature, axial force, material flow and defects using a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model.
Trained two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force histories.
Used the combined modelling framework to map defective and defect-free process windows.
evidence_signal: Experimental validation supported the simulations; ANN predictions achieved R² values of 0.91–0.99, while 60 °C preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to approximately 1100 N.
watch_item: Accuracy is demonstrated within the tested parameter space; transfer to other HDPE grades, tool geometries or operating ranges requires further validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
